title: The Ahwar of Southern Iraq (marshes and Sumerian cities)
summary: The Ahwar is a World Heritage property in southern Iraq inscribed in 2016. It joins four marsh areas of the Tigris-Euphrates delta with the Sumerian city remains of Uruk, Ur and Tell Eridu, which grew in the 4th and 3rd millennia BCE. The marshes were heavily drained from the 1950s and partly restored after 2003.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 4th millennium BCE, when the Sumerian cities began to develop (UNESCO via IUCN). End is the 2016 inscription date.

as_recorded.value: between the 4th and the 3rd millennium BCE

where.modern_name: Ahwar of Southern Iraq (southern Iraq marshes with Uruk, Ur and Tell Eridu)
where.historical_name: Southern Mesopotamia: Sumerian city-states with their marshland hinterland

importance.justification: Links the landscape in which Sumerian cities arose to a still-living marsh refuge of biodiversity.
